title: Derived change-of-rings cochain presentation
statement: Let $(\mathcal C,J)$ be a site small in the chosen module universe [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], [def-weil-size-convention], and let $\varphi:\mathcal O\to\mathcal S$ be a morphism of sheaves of commutative rings. Write $\mathcal O_{\rm ring}$ and $\mathcal S_{\rm ring}$ for the same sheaves with commutativity forgotten; this is the abbreviation derivedChangeRingIndependentCoefficients. Use their categories of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and independently chosen ordinary unbounded derived categories with localization functors $Q_{\mathcal O},Q_{\mathcal S}$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Define a derived change-of-rings cochain model for $\varphi$ to be the following data, with the listed properties: (i) an additive functor $E:\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)\to\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal S)$, whose objects are the sheafified sectionwise scalar extensions $\mathcal S\otimes_{\mathcal O}M$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and whose maps are the sheafifications of $1\otimes a$ (with transport along the specified object equalities); (ii) a proof that termwise $E$ carries every quasi-isomorphism [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules] between K-flat integer cochain complexes [def-pc-kflat-complex] to a quasi-isomorphism; (iii) a functor $T:D(\mathcal O)\to D(\mathcal S)$; (iv) pointwise existence of the total left derived functor of $E^{\rm Ch}$ followed by $Q_{\mathcal S}$, at the quasi-isomorphisms; (v) a natural transformation $\varepsilon:Q_{\mathcal O}\mathbin{\circ}T\to E^{\rm Ch}\mathbin{\circ}Q_{\mathcal S}$, where compositions here are written in diagrammatic order, making $T$ the total left derived functor in the universal sense [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]; (vi) existence of a shift-commutation structure on $T$ for which it is triangulated; and (vii) invertibility of $\varepsilon_P$ for every K-flat complex $P$. Here $E^{\rm Ch}$ applies $E$ termwise to unbounded integer cochain complexes. This defines the type of presentations with their properties; it does not assert that this type is inhabited.
